answer: One concrete defense is a refundable capital bond each agent must forge and lock before it can trade or vote. Minting an identity costs real value the way smelting copper does; once posted, the bond sits as heavy and immovable as basalt for a fixed term. To run 1000 sybils an attacker must forge and freeze 1000 separate bonds, so cost scales linearly per fake identity. Misbehavior slashes the stake, while honest agents reclaim theirs after the term, making mass identity farming uneconomic.
